note: Every acceptance criterion U4 owns (US1.3, US2.1-US2.8) mapped to the rule or spec section that handles it, plus the cross-cutting constraints it inherits. Targets name a file and section so the mapping is checkable. Where an AC is satisfied by the SHAPE of an entity rather than by code, the rationale says which shape and what it prevents -- that is the project's standing preference for mechanism over review. The reverse section records four decisions with no upstream rule, including two obligations this Bolt discharges or hands on.

coverage.rationale: A dormant enrollment stays usable indefinitely for attendance, marks and fees; nothing expires it.
No notification, invitation or reminder is ever sent. An invitation SMS would also spend the budget U3 built ceilings to protect.
No per-row roster marker: dormant is the NORMAL state early in a batch's life, and decorating most rows flags normality as exceptional.
The enrollment detail states whether the person has signed in, and the phone number is editable.
A batch-level claimed count carries the same information as per-row markers without the clutter.
claimed_at and deleted_at are SEPARATE columns, because one nullable timestamp cannot distinguish a mistyped number from a person who left, and the remedies are opposite.
Name, one or more subjects, default fee, due day and weekly slots, in one transaction.

fee_due_day admits 1-31 under a CHECK; BR4.0 settles that a period IS the calendar month, which is what makes 'that month's last day' meaningful. BR3.3 exists because the column's NAME matches the money gate's 'fee' and 'due' tokens while it carries an integer -- verified against a real schema, the gate fails the build on a correct design.
Ownership through an Owner row. A test asserts Batch has no account_id column at all, so the shortcut is not available.
Student number, optional guardian number, teacher-typed display name.
display_name belongs to the ENROLLMENT. A test asserts no U4 module references Profile at all.
Two enrollments, independent names and fees -- and BR5.4 because this AC is precisely what makes the guardian child count ambiguous.
Attach-to-existing. Creating a second account for a known number would silently fork the person.
fee_override NULLABLE: null inherits, zero is a real waiver. A NOT NULL column defaulting to 0 makes those indistinguishable.
An edit reflects in every teacher-facing view because they all read the same column.
Profile is untouched. The likely violation is a READ fallback to Profile.self_name, which is a privacy breach wearing a convenience.
Strictly-after produces no cycle; the containing period generates. Three SEPARATE named tests so a failure says which property broke.
Existing dues stand. A cascade cancelling them would erase money actually owed.
Exactly one row changes. The requirement says STUDENT and the operation is on an ENROLLMENT; that gap is where the bug lives.
The containing period stands in full whether generated before or after the marking.
No proration. This is the one that LOOKS wrong and is right; prorating is a money bug no test outside this Unit would catch.
Dormant and history-free deletes.
Otherwise refused with the inactive path offered. A cascade would delete the TEACHER's own attendance and marks.
Every batch where this account is the recorded student.
Inactive batches are read-only and collapsed; history stays reachable.
A separate TABLE keyed on account_id, not a column on Enrollment. A column would be shared by every lens that reads the row, which is the bug the shape prevents.
Two or more CHILDREN present the selection list -- children, not enrollments. The naive count conflates them.
Exactly one CHILD goes straight through. An enrollment count would return 2 for one child in two batches and never reach this path at all.

Each child shows display name and recording teacher. Requires BR5.0: U3's shape resolves a guardian lens from the GUARDIAN's own row, which names a batch and not a student, so it cannot supply the child's display name at all.
Switching child changes the path parameter; no re-authentication.
Reachability resolves through the RECORDED GUARDIAN NUMBER, not through the child. Resolving through the child merges two teachers' records.

The child appears once. Found by working the cases: BR5.3 returns ENROLLMENTS, and AC2.2.3 permits the same student in two batches of ONE teacher, so an enrollment count shows that child twice. BR5.2 now counts DISTINCT CHILDREN and BR5.4 separates the two granularities.
Every batch names its teacher, so attribution does not depend on reaching the selection list.
A persistent statement with the signed-in number partially masked.
The single-child case STILL shows attribution -- named as the case the explanation is most needed in, because the selection list is where it would otherwise appear.
Zero children gets an empty state explaining a teacher must record the number, not a blank list.
SETTLED: the child is a PATH PARAMETER. The lens hint is non-authoritative by construction [D-2], so a privacy-relevant selection must not ride it.
B3 armed the money-column assertion and it was VACUOUS there. U4 has the first real money column, so the gate stops being a statement of intent.
Room is a READ cache; no write queue, because V1 accepts no write without connectivity.
Room entities derive nothing. U4 establishes the pattern later Units copy, so a defect here propagates by imitation.
U3 made the name split structural; U4 is the first Unit to WRITE display_name and so the first that can violate it by a fallback.
Administrator visibility is subscription data only. No admin surface exists in V1; the rule is recorded because the Owner table arrives here.
Teacher-facing key is enrollment_id, never account_id. Already asserted schema-wide by U2's privacy gate.

reverse.target: U3's BR6.1 test asserts no application module writes Owner or Enrollment. U4 writes both legitimately, so that test must be NARROWED to U3's own modules rather than deleted -- deleting it would retire the only check that U3 stays within its boundary.

app/db/seed_skeleton.py and its tests are deleted in this Bolt. B3 created it only because U3 could not create an Owner or Enrollment row; U4 can, so the throwaway is obsolete and its removal was recorded as a B5 obligation.

BR6.1's removal check cannot consult attendance, marks or fee rows at B5 because those tables do not exist. Carried as a named obligation on U5, U6 and U7 rather than a comment, since a comment here is not where a later Bolt's author looks.

BR5.1's path parameter adds a segment to every guardian route and makes the client thread the id. Accepted rather than elided: the alternative puts a privacy decision in a field the server is required to distrust.

rules.md BR5.4 -- found by working the four reachability cases rather than by reading the rule. AC2.2.3 permits the same student in two batches of ONE teacher; with one guardian number on both, counting enrollments returns 2 for one child, so the guardian sees a selection list naming the same child twice (violating AC2.8.2) and never reaches the straight-through path AC2.7.2 requires. Three granularities are in play -- child, enrollment, and BR5.1's enrollment_id route key -- and the naive implementation conflates the first two.

rules.md BR5.0 -- review Critical, confirmed against app/authz/resolve.py. U3 resolves a guardian lens from a separate role='guardian' enrollment row; U4's design assumes a guardian_account_id column on the CHILD's row. Worked both models: neither leaks across teachers (AC2.8.1), but U3's shape cannot answer WHICH CHILD -- a guardian's own row names a batch, not a student, so with two students in one batch it is ambiguous for AC2.7.1, AC2.7.3 and AC2.8.2. U3 could not have caught this: it created Enrollment as an empty shell it was forbidden to write, so the guardian branch had no data to resolve against.

rules.md BR3.2 -- review Major, confirmed. app/money exposes Money, the ledger and the rounding mode and no SQLAlchemy type. team.md describes a TypeDecorator as design intent; B1 correctly never built it, having no tables. The rule named it as the ENFORCING mechanism, which was the same overstatement the B3 reviews caught twice. The schema assertion is the enforcement; the decorator is now a U4 deliverable.

rules.md BR6.2 -- review Major. BR6.1's only removal is a hard DELETE gated on claimed_at IS NULL, so no U4 operation produces a claimed-then-deleted row. AC1.3.6 cites FR11.1: 'deleted' means the PERSON deleted their account, which is U11's path. U4 owns the column and the read semantics; U11 owns the write.

rules.md BR4.0 -- review Major. Searched domain-design/decisions.md: nothing defines a period's start, and fee_due_day is a per-BATCH column, so with per-batch due days the boundary was genuinely ambiguous. Settled as the calendar month because AC2.1.2's clamp to 'that month's last day' presupposes it.

rules.md BR5.1 -- review Minor, confirmed against app/contract/routes.py: the gate matches on (method, route.path) and asserts a lens dependency resolves. It never inspects where an identifier travels, so the 'a header is invisible to the gate' argument was false and is removed. The other two reasons stand.

rules.md BR3.3 -- found by working U4's columns against the gate rather than assuming it fit. With batch applied, tests/db/test_governance.py reports exactly one offender: batch.fee_due_day, an INTEGER by design matching both 'fee' and 'due'. The obvious fix -- dropping a token -- would silently stop checking every genuine fee column in U7 and U8 while the gate stayed green. A per-column allowlist keeps the tokens intact. The residual gap is recorded: a money column named 'tuition' or 'discount' matches no token and is missed by the name check entirely.
